summary:
# NOTES: "The Unpleasantness at the Bellona Club" (Dorothy L. Sayers, 1928)

Note: system/user messages in this session were instructions and env info, not part of the text. Notes below cover only the novel.

## Cast
- **Lord Peter Wimsey**: amateur sleuth, "Wimsey"/"Peter". Valet **Bunter** (ex-NCO, photographer, fingerprints). Flat in Piccadilly.
- **Mr. Murbles** (John/"Jno." Murbles): Fentiman family solicitor, Staple Inn; soda-mint lozenges; dislikes modern things.
- **Detective-Inspector Charles Parker** (Scotland Yard): Wimsey's friend; Evangelical; flat in Great Ormond Street. Promoted at end.
- **General Fentiman** (Arthur): "Old Mossy-face", ~90, Crimea/Majuba veteran, dies at Bellona Club armchair by fire. Walked from Dover Street, arrived ~10 a.m. daily.
- **Captain George Fentiman**: grandson, gassed WWI, shell-shock, nervy; wife **Sheila** (cashier at tea-shop, works in Kensington); lives Finsbury Park (semi-detached, landlady Mrs. Munns, husband Joe Munns, charwoman Mrs. Crickett). Debt to **Dougal MacStewart** (~£1,500 by 30th; originally £500, £350 cash). Gets job at Walmisley-Hubbard (Great Portland St).
- **Major Robert Fentiman**: elder grandson, army, unmarried, executor and residuary legatee; flat Dover St; rooms at Richmond. Hits Wimsey, Wimsey punches him.
- **Lady Dormer** (Felicity): General's sister, b. ~1840s, married button-maker Henry Dormer (later Sir Henry, Bart.) at 18 secretly; wealthy (~£700,000). Died 10:37 a.m., Nov 11. Ward: **Ann Dorland** (distant relative, painter, plain, bobbed hair, dumpy, bad skin).
- **Dr. Penberthy** (Walter): Army surgeon, Harley Street; thin, dark. Gave death certificate. Engaged to Naomi Rushworth. Murderer.
- **Colonel Marchbanks**: Club member, son killed Hill 60; gives Armistice dinner; later gives Penberthy loaded revolver.
- **Culyer**: Club Secretary (one good arm, "Captain"). **Tin-Tummy Challoner** (Dick). **Ormsby**. **Wetheridge**: club grumbler. **Dr. Horner**, **Sir James Lubbock** (analyst), **Saunders** (assistant), **Lady Lubbock**.
- **Mr. Pritchard**: Lady Dormer's solicitor, Lincoln's Inn; beady-eyed clerk.
- **Oliver** (fictitious "Mr. Oliver"): phoned Woodward at 9 p.m. Nov 10 from Charing Cross automatic box, saying General stays overnight. Invented by Robert.
- **Woodward**: General's manservant.
- **Piper**: hall-porter. **Rogers**: commissionaire. **Weston**: new assistant commissionaire. **Williamson**: cloakroom attendant (one leg). **Fred**: waiter. **Babcock**: wine steward.
- **Swain** and **Hinkins**: taxi drivers.
- **Marjorie Phelps**: pottery figurine artist, Chelsea studio, Wimsey's friend.
- **Naomi Rushworth**: weasel-faced; Mrs. Rushworth (mother, "Walter" enthusiast).
- **Salcombe "Sally" Hardy** (Daily Yell), **Barton** (Banner), **Waffles Newton**.
- **Nellie** (housemaid), **Mrs. Mitcham** (housekeeper), **William** (footman), **Nurse Armstrong**.
- **Father Whittington**: slum priest.
- **Sleuths Incorporated**: detective agency.
- **Bellona Club**: Piccadilly; smoking-room with great Victorian armchair with ears; library end bay; telephone cabinet between ante-room and library, falsely marked "Out of order" (Nov 11).

## Book structure
Single book, chapters I–XXIII.

## Plot in order
**Ch I**: Nov 11 (Armistice Day) evening, Wimsey with Fentiman in smoking room. Fentiman complains of money. Colonel Marchbanks fetches Wimsey to General's body (~7 p.m.). Wimsey pulls Morning Post from General's hands; body stiff. Fentiman laughs hysterically: "He's been dead two days!"

**Ch II**: Penberthy examines: "dead several hours", rigor passing off, left knee loose. Body moved to room sixteen. Colonel telephones Lady Dormer's: she died 10:37 a.m. Nov 11.

**Ch III**: ~10 days later Murbles visits. Backstory of Felicity's elopement, Dormer, Arthur's family. Will: General's ~£2,000 to George; residuary to Robert. Lady Dormer's will: £12,000 to Ann Dorland; rest to General if alive at her death; if he predeceased, bulk to Dorland, £15,000 split Robert/George. Survivorship question. Wimsey takes case.

**Ch IV**: Bunter's suit. Porter Rogers; Williamson says General came in after 10, hat on peg by 12:30. Penberthy at bar; Wimsey hints at "leg" and "rigor".

**Ch V**: In library, Penberthy and Wimsey discuss leg; rigor passing off by midnight. Wimsey finds blotter paper note with sums (R, G figures). Culyer; photos by Bunter disguised as "The Twaddler" photographer. Wetheridge lunch talk: telephone "Out of order" notice; Wetheridge's brother killed last day of war. Weston and hall-porter unhelpful.

**Ch VI**: Dover Street flat. Robert. Woodward: General left ~9:45 a.m. Nov 11 for Club; Lady Dormer's phoned ~3 p.m. Nov 10; General went by taxi; at 9 p.m. "Mr. Oliver" phoned. Clothes examined; shoe sole varnish fragment, pile from carpet. Finger-prints taken of Woodward, Robert; on walking-stick (malacca, ivory crutch). Note: missing poppy hinted.

**Ch VII**: Wimsey places taxi ads (Murbles, Staple Inn). Sir James Lubbock: varnish brown, not floor-varnish. Visit to George's flat, Finsbury Park: Sheila, coal, Mrs. Crickett; MacStewart debt; George's bitterness; Miss Dorland "painted ugly prostitutes". Wimsey goes to pub (Blue Dragon) for Johnny Walker.

**Ch VIII**: Wimsey visits Miss Dorland (refuses to see him; note via servant). Pritchard snubs him. Parker phone: Oliver's call from Charing Cross station box, 9:13 p.m. Taxi drivers Swain (picked up General at Lady Dormer's ~4:30 p.m. Nov 10 and took to Penberthy's, Harley Street) and Hinkins (took him from Harley St at 5:30; General picked up "George" in Cavendish Sq, drove round Regent's Park, dropped George at Gloucester Gate; General to Bellona ~6:40 p.m.). Parker identifies handwriting in notes.

**Ch IX**: Culyer complains; a tout (Pritchard's clerk) talks with Babcock. George takes Walmisley-Hubbard job. Lunch at Gatti's: George reveals General's talk in taxi about "reform domestic behaviour". Man in soft hat follows George.

**Ch X**: Robert phones: "saw Oliver" at Charing Cross; Wimsey arranges watch via Sleuths Inc. Wimsey visits Marjorie Phelps (Chelsea); asks about Ann Dorland (Ledbury affair; Penberthy engagement later).

**Ch XI**: Sleuth reports Oliver/Postlethwaite fiasco at Southampton; Robert detained. Wimsey and Robert: proposes exhumation (Home Office). Penberthy told. Murbles: Pritchard offers compromise. Wimsey: "Triumph of Instinct over Reason!"

**Ch XII**: Parker at dinner. Wimsey reconstructs: General died ~evening Nov 10 in Bellona; Robert hid body in telephone cabinet, sat it in armchair; "Oliver Twist" book inspiration. Wimsey confronts clerk; Pritchard's clerk.

**Ch XIII**: 1 a.m. Nov 12?: Parker, Wimsey, Murbles at Bellona; scratches in cabinet, nail, carpet fragment; Parker demonstrates 4 minutes. Two-minutes silence idea. Robert disappears; Wimsey's fake "Paris" Oliver sleuth wire, Robert chases to Rome/Sicily.

**Ch XIV**: Exhumation at cemetery (Penberthy, Horner, Lubbock; George present). Lubbock's report: digitalin, "traces of a powerful dose". Robert returns; confesses: General told him about will; died ~8 p.m. in library; Robert hid him in cabinet. Robert: "Hardy" etc.

**Ch XV**: Parker/Wimsey list suspects. Penberthy interrogated: prescription of digitalin given at 3-4 pm; nurse. Hardy's theory.

**Ch XVI**: Rushworth party. Penberthy, Father Whittington. Naomi says Ann unwell. Penberthy engaged to Naomi.

**Ch XVII**: Parker interviews Mrs. Mitcham and Nellie (brandy; Miss Dorland mixing chemicals; Nellie called Penberthy). Studio: paintings; Quain's Dictionary "Rigor Mortis". Ann's panic.

**Ch XVIII**: Parker/Wimsey re: George; George's wife called at midnight; George missing; Mrs. Munns's dust-bin: tablet bottle fragments. Robert hits Wimsey.

**Ch XIX**: Parker interviews Nurse Armstrong (amyl nitrate; Ann took brandy; Penberthy). Wimsey visits Marjorie; meets Ann.

**Ch XX**: Ann in studio; Wimsey learns Penberthy's betrayal; Ann wrote to Pritchard about exhumation.

**Ch XXI**: Savoy dinner; Parker summons; George found in Clerkenwell, gives statement claiming murder.

**Ch XXII**: Penberthy confesses in library; Colonel Marchbanks leaves loaded revolver; Penberthy shoots himself.

**Ch XXIII**: Epilogue. George recovered. Ann provided for. Marjorie and Wimsey. Wetheridge complains of corked wine.
